# Phase-3 absorption ledger — concept level

Every meaningful current technical concept of every Bible unit, with its disposition, destination and the TARGET check that decided it. Generated from `audit/data/bible/records/*.json`.

## titlepage (front)

The title page frames the work as a revision-bounded account of CNA, a C++23 reimplementation of the XNA 4.0 programming model, pinned to a development snapshot with its last tag and product version. The identity facts (snapshot, tag, product version) are already on the site's releases page; the book title, edition name and author credit are book furniture.

## preface (front)

The preface summarises what CNA is at the pin (C++23 XNA 4.0 reimplementation, independent platform/audio/renderer axes, 25 identities over 21 families), the sibling repositories, the evidence distinctions used throughout, and the C API status. Most facts are current and already on the site; the stated reason for the C API release-gate failure is stale at TARGET, and the book-structure and AI-production passages are book narrative. The not-a-game framing, sibling roles and evidence distinctions now live on the new foundations pages.

## ch01-cna-and-xna (chapter)

Introduces CNA as a C++ reimplementation of XNA 4.0: a translation target rather than a loader, three engineering problems (API, runtime, GPU), the README's goals, the evidence-vector stance, the negative space, verification instruments (FNA harness, Windows 7 reproducer, strict check, oracle), the Song/FNA case, the release and phase model, and the Ms-PL licence. Updated for d6e9ff05 but partly stale: it still says CNA has no content builder or reader bootstrap and overstates the strict check. The site had the version model, oracle and negative space in pieces; the translation-target framing, authority split, Song case, goals and licence detail were missing and now form the CNA and XNA 4.0 page.

Maps CNA's sibling repositories (sharp-runtime, easy-gl, free-direct, xna4-spec, cna-samples, cna-examples), how CMake wires them, and each sibling's own boundary. The wiring is current (with a new CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_ROOT override and reworded messages); several sibling facts are stale (sharp-runtime scope, plan statuses, sample counts, cna-examples maturity, easy-gl's MIGRATION.md). ## ch03-language-conventions-cnaext (chapter)

The house-style chapter: match FNA/XNA exactly, two namespace families, the CNAEXT marker and its strict check, property/alias/event/interface/IDisposable/visibility translations, module layout, no shims, Doxygen, missing dependencies and the per-file checklist. It is alpha.1-era text never re-synchronised: examples drifted (Color has no GetTypeName, SkinnedEffect throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException, header counts, ReadChar semantics, XNA-wins rule). The site's conventions page had the rules and how they are held; the worked examples, the translation reasoning and the drift between written rules and code were missing and are on the new conventions page.

## ch04-configuring-building (chapter)

The unit is the command-line configuration chapter: prerequisites, submodules, the default Linux build, a CMake option table, the generated version header, Windows native and MinGW routes, Android and Emscripten, system SDL, FFmpeg and Draco, and how to verify a build. Much of it is stale at TARGET (a GCC 12 floor, --target CNA, CNA_TEST_DISPLAY ":0", project-wide sanitizer flags, mandatory FFmpeg, libswscale at run time). docs/building.html and the Development build pages already held the option facts; the residue (per-route toolchains, test execution and what a green result proves, the ccache launcher rule, the Windows DLL copy, Emscripten Node versus browser evidence) went into a new build-routes deep dive.

## ch05-first-game (chapter)

A worked first game (skeleton, movement, clamped bounce with sound, rectangle collision, renderer independence). The API calls are current at TARGET, but several explanations were imprecise (the 'content model' framing, frame-rate independence under fixed step, viewport semantics) and the bounce example replayed its sound every update. libcna.com already had the skeleton and lifecycle basics in getting-started, the game-loop guide and tutorials 03-16; the line-by-line reasoning, the CNAEXT-versus-XNA portability notes and the strict Intersects edge case were missing and now live on a new walkthrough deep dive with syntax-checked programs.

## ch06-game-lifecycle (chapter)

A dense account of Game (events, properties, override points, Exit/Exiting, disposal versus destruction), the clock (catch-up, IsRunningSlowly, ResetElapsedTime), GameTime, components, services, GameWindow, GraphicsDeviceManager, supporting types and the exception boundary. Most mechanics are current at TARGET, but the browser loop (now Asyncify, Run returns), controller and audio teardown, GameWindow's SDL coupling, several XNA-parity claims (ExitingEventArgs, ResetElapsedTime) and renderer counts are stale. The Development internals pages already traced startup, frame and shutdown in depth; the API-semantics residue, edge cases, XNA 4.0 comparisons and evidence caveats went into five framework deep dives plus two additive expansions of the game-loop guide.

## ch07-math-conventions (chapter)

Teaches the math conventions (right-handed basis, row vectors, application-order products, [0,1] depth, clip-space W, ToColumnMajor), the vector/matrix/quaternion operation groups, bounding-volume and curve boundaries, Color packing and degenerate-input policy. The alpha.1-era text predates the XNA oracles, the ties-to-even colour rounding and XNA-IL comparisons; several stated defects are narrower or broader than written (frustum ray, curve Step). libcna.com already had deep maintainer internals and member tables; the XNA-behaviour comparison, conventions and degenerate-input semantics went into six framework deep dives.

## ch08-geometry-color-layout (chapter)

Explains where CNA's C++ value layout departs from XNA's value types (Color's vtables and 24-byte size, IVertexType, the internal vertex-stream structs), plane half-spaces and the aliased plane transform, bounding-volume conventions, Rectangle edge ownership, Color counts and packing, curve extrapolation, split exception families and what the tests prove. Its counts (818 tests, 7 streams, 'no oracle'), the Ritter reading of CreateFromPoints and several defect descriptions are stale at TARGET. The site had layout and failure-map notes on the math internals page; the exact semantics, XNA comparisons and workarounds are now on the framework deep dives.

## ch09-module-monorepo (chapter)

The unit explains CNA's physical module layout: location as ownership, the module set, the cna_add_module factory and include roots, construction exceptions, renderer families as modules, module-owned examples, the no-loss migration and how to read a source path. At TARGET the module count (fifteen) and cna_build_flags are stale and several exceptions changed. The Development repository pages already held the inventory and edges; the reasoning, the naming traps, the partition blind spots, the example and golden ownership and a recreated ownership diagram went into a new module-architecture deep dive.

## ch10-boundaries-enforcement (chapter)

An alpha.1-era chapter on why CNA keeps three static-archive cycles, its umbrella targets, narrow aliases, the minimal-link module probes and their negative contracts, the Ninja caveat, include reachability and header self-containment, the partition guards and a safe boundary-change procedure. At TARGET there are fifteen probes, the build-flags target is cna_build_config, the HEADLESS and Vulkan closures require single-renderer mode, and the reachability and self-containment scripts are stale and unwired. The Development pages had the edges and a short Ninja note; the reasoning, the per-probe contracts, the CI reality and the violation symptoms went into a new boundaries deep dive.

## ch11-dependencies-tools (chapter)

The unit classifies how dependencies are acquired (submodules, in-tree sources, siblings, fetches, host packages), the configure-time SDL build, host-package gates, the sibling contract, renderer dependency asymmetry, build-tree consumption and the C package, then the CnaTests corpus, examples, presets and the authority classes of developer tools. At TARGET the submodule set, the FFmpeg omission model, the preset set and the sanitizer presets changed and there is no in-tree wgpu-native area. The Development pages had pins and overrides; the reproducibility reasoning, composition, failure states, sibling details and the evidence classes went into two new deep dives.

## ch12-graphicsdevice (chapter)

Alpha.1-era chapter on the shared GraphicsDevice contract: construction and windows, public state, viewport/scissor, Clear/Present/Reset, the manager event model, render-target and vertex bindings, draws, readback, resources, adapters and extensions. Many claims are stale at TARGET: construction and disposal are now transactional, Clear throws for missing planes, Present and Vector4 Clear overloads exist, redundant target binding is a no-op, readback is HiDef-only and generic, adapters use the platform layer. The Development pages already carried construction, render-target binding and draw validation; two new deep dives now hold the rest.

## ch13-spritebatch (chapter)

Partly synchronised chapter on SpriteBatch, SpriteSortMode, SpriteEffects and SpriteFont with selected defects. Much of it is contradicted at TARGET: the rasterizer argument is honoured, states are applied at End for deferred modes, positions and glyphs stay fractional in the shared layer, sorting reproduces XNA's unstable quicksort, SpriteEffects is a flags enum, the SpriteFont reader exists and misuse throws InvalidOperationException. The site had overload lists and a sort-mode tutorial; three new deep dives and a SpriteBatch guide expansion now carry the state, sorting, batching and text-layout semantics.

## ch14-textures-rendertargets (chapter)

Textures, render targets and buffers: format admission, Texture2D/3D/Cube transfer and readback, FromStream, cube targets, RenderTargetUsage, vertex/index buffers and layouts. Partly stale against TARGET (core graphics files are byte-identical to the Bible pin, so several claims were already wrong there): FromStream accepts only PNG/JPEG/GIF via stb_image, typed and template transfers exist, RenderTargetCube::Dispose guards bound targets, unchanged bindings are a no-op, Headless/Software/cube-readback and buffer-options claims changed. The site had the user guides, tutorial 152 and the resources internals page; it lacked per-resource profile tables, the transfer-window and CPU-shadow semantics, cube/volume readback, usage contents rules, buffer option handling and the lifetime figure, now on five deep dives.

## ch15-stock-effects (chapter)

Explains the Effect base (stock versus compiled mode, collections, pass selection, cloning), the stock-parameter boundary, EffectParameter storage, the GpuDrawParams packet and the five stock geometry effects with worked uses and their defect history. Partly stale at TARGET: BasicEffect now exposes XNA's 21-parameter graph, compiled effects have nine opt-in families, parameters of compiled effects are type-checked, Fresnel is per vertex, Software lights and honours PreferPerPixelLighting, and the draw packet is far larger. The site's Effects System page had the surface and property tables; the object model, parameter semantics, exact formulas and verification history went into two new deep dives.

## ch16-state-objects (chapter)

State objects: presets, properties, what reaches the renderer, per-family support and worked examples. Its central thesis is stale at TARGET: states use a shared payload with XNA's freeze-on-bind rule (assignment aliases, mutation after binding throws, copy construction gives a new mutable state), and MultiSampleAntiAlias, AddressW, the device MultiSampleMask, EasyGL reference stencil, mip-aware EasyGL filtering, sampler mip controls on twelve families, SDL_GPU and Software anisotropy and D3D12/Software scissor all changed. The site's guide covered presets and usage; identity, freeze, submission timing and per-family hook coverage are now on the state-objects deep dive, with an expansion in the guide.

## ch17-shaders-four-answers (chapter)

Separates CNA's four shader routes — renderer-owned stock semantics, DIRECTX9 recompilation of Microsoft's stock sources (61/66 bytecode match), compiled Effect Framework bytecode, and the renderer-specific ShaderEffect — and gives the ShaderEffect object contract, its 3D path and arbitrary-layout fix. Partly stale at TARGET: nine (not eight) opt-in compiled-effect families, WebGPU, Vulkan, SDL_GPU and Direct3D 11/12 now consume ShaderEffect in 3D draws with reflection-based uniforms, diagnostics accessors exist and disposal releases the program. The site's Shader Effects and Effects System pages had the usage and per-renderer input table; the route comparison, compiled-effect internals and object contract went into two new deep dives with the figure recreated.

## ch18-vertex-streams-capabilities (chapter)

Follows a draw from public vertex values through declarations, buffers and bindings (semantic composition, minimum-offset fold, validation order) and explains what capability answers, interface defaults and the unsupported-3D policy do and do not guarantee. Partly stale at TARGET: 19 capability members (not 13), null bindings refused, repeated semantics remapped rather than dropped, InvalidOperationException for a missing effect, renderer-dependent range validation, a non-zero element hash and more stream sizes. Tutorial 101 already carried the capability table, polarity and policy; the vertex contract, interface-default shapes and portable-claim checklist were missing and form two new deep dives.

## ch19-renderer-contract (chapter)

Defines the internal renderer contract: default-body kinds, resource ownership, null factories, borrowed handles, the presentation, swap-interval, format and readback matrices, resource and draw defaults, targets, clears, viewport and scissor, capability polarity and recovery hooks. About half of its family rows were stale at 009d40f5 (moves now transfer registration, rebinding is a no-op, clears throw on missing aspects, readback is HiDef-only and refused while a target is bound, many listed defects fixed). The site had strong device and resource internals but no consolidated contract, presentation or clear/viewport matrix; three deep dives now carry it.

## ch20-selection-identity (chapter)

Distinguishes known identities, the compiled set, the default and the runtime selection, lists the 25 identities with their families and boundaries, and explains why an identity is not a maturity claim. Current at 009d40f5 except that the latch closes on the first successful renderer creation. libcna.com already carried nearly all of it (the runtime-selection guide, the renderers page and the selection internals); the evidence-stage lesson, the process-wide rationale and a recreated identity-to-family diagram were added to the renderer-contract deep dive.

## ch21-opengl-fixed-profiles (chapter)

Although filed under an old fixed-function title, the unit at this revision describes the five current EasyGL profiles: what the family shares, how profile data differs, transfers and state, effects and the evidence boundary. It is current at 009d40f5 except that the stock corpus is now shared with OPENGL4 and redundancy filtering is narrower than a general state cache. No retired renderer is discussed. The site already covered identity and profiles; the transfer, state, evidence-transfer and per-profile role material went to the EasyGL profiles deep dive.

## ch22-opengl-programmable (chapter)

Audits the EasyGL family's bug history and semantics (MRT, base vertex, occlusion, wireframe, fog, colour masks, targets, SpriteBatch index ceiling, back buffer, recovery, viewport, stencil, buffer shadows, clears, tests, Xvfb and oracle evidence) and contrasts OPENGL4 and PORTABLEGL. Much is stale at 009d40f5: base vertex, index wrap, clear depth bit, wireframe design, cube and volume formats, SetDataRaw readback and OPENGL4's dispatch all changed. The site had thorough EasyGL and OpenGL4 internals but not these semantics; two EasyGL deep dives now carry them.

## ch23-native-modern-gpu (chapter)

Explains the four modern explicit-API renderers with a Vulkan focus: blend and stencil defect history, occlusion-query mechanics, ordered clears and usage, swapchain format and present modes, frames in flight, deferred-present readback, descriptor pools, Metal's refusals and the evidence tiers. Partly stale at 009d40f5: the 512-set ceiling, the missing SetSwapInterval override, the unresolved depth-bias failure and the coverage gap are all contradicted. The site had one-line Vulkan internals coverage of swapchain, present and snapshots, and strong Metal and capability-polarity coverage in tutorials 109 and 101; the depth was written into two Vulkan deep dives and an evidence-tiers page.

## legacy-webgpu (fragment)

Older WebGPU campaign narrative: native 2D baseline, pixel-assertion lessons, PbrEffect, render targets, cube targets, mip generation, the BC gap, three former limitations and an open-items list. Largely stale at 009d40f5: MRT, stencil baking, wireframe, custom SpriteBatch and WGSL effects, cube mips and MSAA, BC upload, the browser route and a non-sRGB surface policy all exist. Tutorial 132 already covered build, capabilities and formats; current renderer semantics and the historical lessons were written into a WebGPU deep dive.

## legacy-sdlgpu (fragment)

Older SDL_GPU campaign narrative: dependency argument, SDL_gpu shader convention and Y-flip, skinned palette, runtime GLSL ShaderEffect and the .cnj boundary, pipeline snapshots and hashing, draw order, present timing, validation findings, render-target lifetime, MRT, usage, Texture3D cycling, swapchain recovery and open items. Partly stale at 009d40f5: the palette is now a texture, back-buffer depth follows DepthFormat, instancing exists, cube MSAA uses per-face textures and occlusion creation throws. The Development internals page already held much of the mechanism; the rationale, tests and corrections went into two SDL_GPU deep dives.

## ch28-modern-direct3d (chapter)

A dense chapter on the three Direct3D renderers: DIRECTX9's oracle-driven XNA fidelity (stock-effect bytecode, profile enforcement, lost devices, sprite projection fixes), the DXGI renderers' lifetimes, presentation, viewport, clear and readback behaviour, Direct3D 12 frames in flight and descriptor heaps, MRT and cube finalisation, the ShaderEffect contract and HeadlessEXT. Much of it is stale at 009d40f5: descriptor heaps now grow, D3D12 drawing is pipelined, D3D12 has scissor and back-buffer readback, DXGI presentation modes and intervals and depth formats are honoured, and ShaderEffect uses reflection. libcna.com had only renderer-table rows, Tutorial 103 and the oracle maintainer page; five deep-dive pages now carry the current depth.

## ch29-windows-2d (chapter)

Explains why DIRECT2D (native Direct2D over Direct3D 11) and GDI (Win32 presentation of a CPU raster) are different delivery stacks, how GDI composes the Software family's 2D code, and what their evidence and release gate prove. The alpha.1-era text is broadly right on architecture but stale on workflows (both native jobs are manual), on test counts and on comparison-scene advice. libcna.com had only renderer-table rows and one internals paragraph; a new deep dive now carries the device, format, blend, recovery, presentation and evidence depth.

## ch30-vector-rasterizers (chapter)

Despite its label this unit is an in-depth study of SDL_RENDERER: the execution-time 2D boundary, its single capability, the audit fixes, the open Wrap/Mirror decision, native versus emulated XNA features, readback coordinates and Xvfb evidence. Updated for the later pin, it is mostly current but wrong at 009d40f5 on public Clear (now throws), buffer-argument ordering, redundant rebinding, readback under scaling and the test-display default. libcna.com had only table rows and scattered cross-renderer mentions; a new deep dive carries the contract.

## ch31-web-dom-renderers (chapter)

Compares the three non-WebGL browser renderers by object model: Canvas 2D pixels, pooled CSS elements and retained SVG, with their capability answers, 3D refusal policies and evidence tiers. Mostly current, but it describes the DOM renderers' targets as DOM-backed (they are canvas-backed), omits the opt-in host contract suites and counts thirteen capabilities. Tutorial 105 already covered choice and performance; a new deep dive adds the source-level object models, refusals and evidence matrix.

## ch34-xnb-container (chapter)

Alpha.1-era chapter on the XNB envelope: header, four-valued compression, LZX state, the reader table and name parser, limits and the length cross-check. Stale at TARGET where it calls LZ4 a deliberate refusal and presents the both-directions length rule as general. The site's XNB guide, Tutorial 147 and the runtime internals held the header, limits and maxFileSize caveat; the LZX framing and oracle, name-parser details, per-limit enforcement sites and the run-time versus build-time length rules now live on a new deep dive.

## ch35-xnb-type-readers (chapter)

Updated for the Bible's pin: registration systems, the ContentReader session, type erasure and reader-by-reader wire contracts with evidence. Much of the per-reader validation text is stale at TARGET because the runtime readers now share the canonical decoders: SpriteFont list lengths, exact texture level sizes, Curve counts, SoundEffect loops and index divisibility are checked; Texture2D accepts the whole classic format range and can keep DXT compressed; Texture3D refuses DXT; Model tags are partly accepted; Game registers the built-ins. The site held the reader inventory and registration; the session semantics and per-reader contracts now live on two new deep dives.

## ch36-cnj-format (chapter)

Rewritten for the Bible's pin into a CNB chapter with a closing CNJ section: container contract, schemas, compression and mmap, runtime integration, CNJ's role and tooling. Mostly current; wrong in a few details at TARGET (CRC over stored bytes not logical data, custom ids hashed case-sensitively, no sorting in the writer, the type check after construction). The site's CNB Format page already held the container at byte level; the CNJ relationship, parser split and path rules now live on a new CNJ deep dive.

## ch37-content-robustness (chapter)

Alpha.1-era chapter on content hardening: where limits are enforced, trust rules for names versus internal references, recursion bounds, fuzzing, differential oracles, error normalisation and remaining asymmetries. Several asymmetries are closed at TARGET (SpriteFont list lengths, exact Texture3D/TextureCube levels, glTF validation, wrapped glTF errors through Load<Model>) while new ones appear on reading (untyped object path without a depth guard, late LZX length check). The site held individual limits on several pages; a cross-format hostile-input deep dive now carries the whole picture.

## ch38-models-meshes (chapter)

Updated chapter on the Model/ModelMesh/ModelMeshPart runtime: draw contract, part/effect bookkeeping, thread-local scratch, model content routes, copy and ownership semantics, hand-built graphs, the root-bone constructor and collection rules. Largely current, but several claims are stale at TARGET: Draw throws InvalidOperationException, a concurrency test exists, empty names throw ArgumentNullException, the CNJ route computes bounding spheres, XNB keeps tags and uses the root-index constructor, a fifth (.cnb) route exists and copy/unload behaviour is test-pinned. The site had the user-level API and examples; the contract depth now lives on the model runtime and skinning deep dives.

## ch39-gltf-import-core (chapter)

Alpha.1-era chapter on the shared glTF import core: parser and validation boundary, scene flattening, mesh groups, unit scale, extraction, the extension registry and failure/lifetime rules. Mostly still true in shape, but stale in detail: the core is three times larger, the offline orchestration is reused by cna-content and gltf_to_cnb, no-scene files walk root nodes, effects are shared, samplers are imported, missing normals are computed and Load<T> now wraps extraction errors in ContentLoadException. The site had the user-level limits table; the internals now live on the glTF import deep dive.

## ch40-gpu-packing (chapter)

Alpha.1-era chapter on the glTF vertex-byte ABI: the stride table, the vtable-inflation bug behind typed/raw upload, index narrowing, the seven topologies, tangents, mirroring and hard limits. The layouts themselves are current, but selection changed (material-model rule, coloured PBR at 60/80), the table is now canonical data queried by upload and morphing, unknown strides are refused, the index alignment hazard is fixed and missing normals are computed. None of this was on the site; it now lives on the vertex packing deep dive.

## ch41-skinning-animation (chapter)

Current in substance; TARGET adds load-time bind-pose palettes, explicit scene/palette maps, the half-open STEP rule, refusal of skins over 72 joints, rigid-clip target spaces and shared keyframe aliases. ## ch42-cnj-model-toolchain (chapter)

Updated chapter on cna_tool_gltf_to_cnj, the per-type version-2 Model envelope, sidecar validation, offline/runtime parity, the dual-texture occlusion remap and route choice. Mostly current; TARGET differs in that the conversion is shared with cna-content and gltf_to_cnb, unknown strides are refused, morph sidecars are strictly validated with a tangent trailer, cameras are not carried in CNJ, and the dual-texture route is reached only by unlit materials. Tutorial 111 had the user workflow; reader rules, sidecar edges, parity tests and the remap derivation now live on the CNJ toolchain deep dive.

## ch43-gltf-conformance (chapter)

Updated chapter on the glTF evidence system: specification pin, generated 148-asset corpus, the L0-L7 ladder, renderer-owned L7 campaigns, Khronos comparisons, the append-only defect ledger, loss reporting and milestone statuses. Largely current at TARGET; corrections add L0/Perf/Ledger/Tool CTest entries, the CI scope, the 13-asset reference subset, a ninth ledger record and the restated open ROBUST rows. The site had only one line of counts on the verification page; the full evidence model now lives on the glTF conformance deep dive.

## ch44-input-system (chapter)

Input chapter (keyboard, mouse, logical coordinates, gamepad, touch, TextInputEXT, CNA::Input extensions, focus, platform limits). Its architecture model (bridge-fed InputManager read by GetState) and many renderer, cursor, sensor and haptic statements are stale even at its own pin: TARGET publishes keyboard/mouse snapshots from platform services, twelve cursor descriptions, a WindowId renderer registry and self-acquiring sensor/haptic subsystems. The site had strong internals (Input internals) but lacked the public contract detail; four new deep dives now carry it.

## ch45-audio-system (chapter)

Audio chapter: selection axis, SDL3 and ALSA mixers, SoundEffect and 3D formulas, dynamic streaming, XACT objects, XNB formats, corrections history, open limits, microphone and evidence. Mostly current; stale points are the SDL_INIT_AUDIO pin (now per-stream), XNB decoding route (now CNA's own decoder), RendererDetails, wave-bank streaming, SoundBank disposal and the microphone BufferDuration defect (fixed). Audio engine internals and the guide already held the mixer and device material; two new deep dives carry the caller semantics, XACT runtime and evidence.

## ch46-media-system (chapter)

Alpha.1-era media chapter: Song contract, MediaLibrary metadata, queue and playback, visualization, video contract, platform limits. Largely current in substance, but the video platform story (link-time failure, Windows guard defect) is obsolete, Opus is not decodable, the visualization normalization and test claims are wrong, and a video-track switch always recreates the texture. Media internals and the FFmpeg page already held the scan, queue and decoder internals; a new public-contract deep dive holds the rest.

## ch50-storage (chapter)

Storage chapter updated for the Bible pin: device contract, root resolution, container operations, containment, the untested glob, ignored FileShare and the exception boundary. Its root chain (SDL_GetPrefPath first) and its claim that tests cover ordinary read/write are wrong at TARGET. The Storage guide and the very deep storage internals page already carried nearly everything; complete-read guidance, exact wildcard semantics and disposal/sharing consequences were added to the guide as an expansion.

## ch51-networking (chapter)

Alpha.1-era networking chapter: session types, SystemLink/ENet transport, discovery, migration, delivery mapping, compatibility quirks, the shared async action and lifetime hardening. Several claims are stale at TARGET: maxGamers is forwarded (not 69), PlayerMatch/Ranked/JoinInvited are refused, ReadColor is fixed, opcode 0x07 exists and LocalWithLeaderboards adds no persistence. Tutorial 97 and the net internals page covered most mechanics; the wire and discovery protocol tables, trust model, delivery table, properties-indexer quirk, web topology and the hardening history now live on a new deep dive.

## ch52-avatar (chapter)

Avatar chapter: the faithfully inert XNA avatar API, the SkinnedModelEXT contract and palette maths, lighting, appearance and wardrobe, the content format and its traps, the open garment interpenetration and the renderer evidence. Almost entirely current (one static-vs-instance event correction and a retired-family remark). libcna.com had only passing mentions (Tutorial 123, Tutorial 57, the XNA compatibility page), so the substance now lives on a new Avatars deep dive.

## ch53-sharp-runtime-overview (chapter)

Alpha.1-era overview of sharp-runtime as a project in its own right: scale, include roots, the opt-in Object, String/Exception adaptation, EventHandler/MulticastAction, TimeSpan and fail-fast collections, the Task model, permanent scope boundaries, the modular build and CI scope. Every count is stale at sharp-runtime next @ 41b918c9 (1,097 headers, 44 modules/47 names, 81 CNA includes, three Object subclasses, ten CI configurations) and the serialization boundary narrowed. libcna.com had only the ecosystem summary, the build seam and Tutorial 89; the runtime semantics now live on four new sharp-runtime deep dives.

## ch54-components-consumption (chapter)

Alpha.1-era explanation of how CNA consumes modular sharp-runtime: directories vs components, include vs link closure, standalone vs embedded selection, the sibling contract, cna_link_sharp_runtime, component tests and upgrade rules. At TARGET CNA passes its closure in SHARP_RUNTIME_COMPONENTS, so the embedded build is no longer All; the closure has 13(+1) components and 21 call sites. The CNA-side seam was already on the third-party-dependencies page; the registry mechanics, per-module table and upgrade rules are on the new components page.

## ch55-object-model (chapter)

Alpha.1-era chapter on sharp-runtime's real object model: opt-in Object, String as a static vocabulary, exceptions under std::exception, RAII-first lifetime and GC stubs, three delegate representations and RTTI-only Type/Activator. Mostly current at sharp-runtime next @ 41b918c9; stale details are the Object subclass count, Delegate equality, Activator overloads and DateTime::Now(). The site had only the IDisposable pattern (Tutorial 89) and the event token idiom; the full model is now on the object-model deep dive.

## ch57-parity-philosophy (chapter)

Alpha.1-era chapter on sharp-runtime's parity target and permanent deviations: three outcomes, reflection, GC, delegates, serialization, interop, cryptography, IDisposable and ReaderWriterLockSlim, exception hierarchy, frozen naming, platform limits and __int128. Mostly current at 41b918c9, but serialization narrowed (SerializationInfo value store) and three further permanent deviations exist. The site mentioned the non-goals only in one Tutorial 89 callout; the full treatment is on the parity-and-verification deep dive.

## ch59-easygl-metagl (chapter)

Alpha.1-era chapter on the easy-gl/meta-gl stack: ownership split, WebGL-aware initialization, the per-feature table, meta-gl's typed surface and terminate contract, API corrections, RAII helpers, two context-loss tiers, mock-loader tests, limitations and the history rewrite. Its pins (0b46d35c/571d3a62) are too old for 009d40f5 (Rgba16, exception model), CNA does not use Device::supports/require, DesktopEsTier is internal and CNA itself adopts RecoverableResource. libcna.com had only a sibling summary and CNA-side EasyGL internals; the library layer is now one deep dive.

## ch70-oracles (chapter)

Surveys CNA's oracles (real-XNA image corpus, tolerance policy, project goldens, point samples, the FNA value harness, independent oracles) and argues for choosing authority before tolerance. The XNA corpus itself was already covered in depth by the verification and xna-oracle pages; the golden harness semantics, tolerance distribution, point-sample counts, FNA comparator semantics, independent-oracle patterns and authority hierarchy are new on the oracles deep dive. Counts and renderer names were stale and corrected; the policy table belonged to a retired family.

## ch74-migration-guide (chapter)

A process chapter for porting XNA/FNA games: freeze a baseline, translate mechanically, map assets and shaders to concrete routes, choose renderers by evidence, make services and timing explicit, verify in rungs and troubleshoot by boundary. Several content and renderer facts were stale (CNA writes XNB/CNB, LZ4 is decoded, 14 compiled-effect identities, five model routes, run-time renderer selection). ## ch75-blupi-case-study (chapter)

An alpha.1-era case study of free-direct's call-site audits of the free-eggbert (Speedy Eggbert 2) reconstruction and Planet Blupi, plus a native-CNA feasibility study for Free Eggbert. The sibling facts were re-read at free-direct 934f72f and free-eggbert 7ea63d1 and the CNA facts (CNJ colour key, Song extensions, SDL_mixer MIDI options, default timestep) at TARGET; naming and a few details were corrected. The site had only one-line mentions of free-direct and nothing on these audits; they now live on a new porting case-studies page next to the Speedy Blupi 2013 port.

## ch76-xna4-spec-auditing (chapter)

Explains how to audit CNA's XNA surface against xna4-spec and the reference assemblies, the five-layer reading of the 331/3,627 census, and worked audits of Ray and Viewport. Mostly current, but Ray's boxed Equals now exists, the default Viewport depth range is 0..0, and the TitleSafeArea question is settled by XNA's own IL. The site had the census numbers and the authority rule; the method, the per-category census table and the worked audits are new on a practice deep dive.

## appendix-i-native-c-api (appendix)

A short appendix on the experimental native C API: ABI 0.29.0 and its independence from the product version, results and thread-local errors, handles and ownership, strings and callbacks, the generated coverage inventory, route families, packaging and the release gate. Mostly current (the modules/c-api tree is unchanged since the source's pin), but it calls the headers C17, understates the buffer protocol, omits that no route offers a thread queue, and its gate account needs the measured two-unmet result. libcna.com already covered the build, history, programming model and internals in depth; two reference deep dives now carry the contract residue (admission, buffers, retention, device lifetimes, route families) and the evidence and gate semantics.

## aux-audit (aux)

The manuscript's curated source audit at CNA 7a64362e (pre-alpha.1), with alpha.1 and d6e9ff05 pointers: headline structural findings F-001..F-038, the subsystem matrix, a contradiction log of CNA's own documentation (C-001..C-019) and ten undocumented defects. The chapter packages already put nearly all of its current substance on the site, corrected to 009d40f5; many pin-era facts are now false (SpriteBatch truncation, by-value state, Game not registering XNB readers, zero concepts). Re-checked at TARGET, three CNA documentation defects survive (C-010, C-011, C-018) and are recorded as issue candidates; the renderer-versus-backend vocabulary and the name rule were added to the glossary.

## aux-editorial-audit (aux)

The 2026-08-12 editorial audit of the book: measured baseline, structural audit, evidence vocabulary, renderer terminology, a per-topic contradiction map, stale-number and example policies, diagram, index, accessibility and production plans, and a closure log. The book-process parts are historical. The claims-discipline parts were checked against the site: the vocabulary, the evidence vector and most contradiction-map boundaries are already on the compatibility and verification pages. The universal-word scopes, the four kinds of number and the five kinds of example were missing and were added to the compatibility-and-evidence deep dive. One boundary (the Effect bytecode constructor throws) is false at 009d40f5.

## aux-audit-alpha1-delta (aux)

The bounded alpha.1 delta audit (interval ae0be4b5..v0.1.0-alpha.1): release/version architecture, the 50-identity registry, platform and audio axes, compiled effects, the C API and its two reproduced alpha.1 build failures, and twelve CNA documentation contradictions. The site already covers the alpha.1 facts as history and the 009d40f5 state; most tag-era defects are fixed. Residue added: the unenforced sharp-runtime revision recorded for alpha.1 (releases page) and the surviving 137-versus-140 L7 wording (issue candidate).

## aux-audit-content-xnb-cnj (aux)

Alpha.1-era research audit (CNA 7a64362e, 2026-08-11) of ContentManager, the XNB container, type readers, CNJ and content robustness, with a per-reader table and a critique of CNA's own content documents. The content deep dives already carry nearly all current substance, and many audited facts changed by 009d40f5 (Game registers readers, 61 readers, LZ4 decoded, no weak texture cache, ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder, EnumTypeReader, all surface formats). Residue added: the in-tree proof of custom XNB readers and of fresh-manager registration.

## aux-audit-graphics-core-effects (aux)

Alpha.1-era research audit (CNA 7a64362e, 2026-08-11) of GraphicsDevice, resources, state objects, stock and custom effects, SpriteBatch/SpriteFont, graphics-ext and the renderer interface, plus a critique of CNA's own graphics documents. The graphics and renderer deep dives already carry nearly all current substance, and many audited facts changed at 009d40f5 (state freezing, compiled effects, float sprite destinations, multi-renderer builds, 19 capabilities). Residue added: where GetMaxTextureDimension really comes from, and why RenderPipelineSettings is not a GraphicsDevice member.

## aux-audit-platforms (aux)

Alpha.1-era research audit (CNA 7a64362e) of platform support: an evidence ladder per platform, renderer gates per platform, sixty facts on toolchains, Wine, MSVC, Apple, CI, web, Android and how platform code is distributed, CNA-document contradictions and a book plan. Much of it is stale at 009d40f5 (a real platform layer with seven implementations, 25 renderers, iOS and macOS CI, fixed CI lanes). The platform deep dives already carry the current material. Residue added: the native Linux controller-mapping database, the phone back-buffer orientation rule and the 32-bit arithmetic lane.

## aux-audit-renderer-catalog (aux)

Pre-alpha.1 research audit (CNA 7a64362e) profiling every renderer identity of that time: platform gates, dependencies, shader pipelines, the IGraphicsRenderer contract, capability polarity, verification tiers, facts and contradictions. Roughly half of it concerns retired renderer families. The current half is already on the renderer deep dives, the Development graphics pages and the rendering guide, mostly in corrected form (25 identities, 19 capabilities, 17 interfaces, WebGPU browser route, SDL_shadercross). The residue published is the list of contract comments that still lag the code at TARGET and CNA's defaults rule quoted beside the missing-vertex-input analysis.

## aux-audit-renderer-draw-path-matrix (aux)

Pre-alpha.1 static matrix of the renderer families' effect-aware draw routes, RenderTarget2D factories and real MRT and occlusion-query support, with the capability over-claims it exposed. Half the rows are retired families. The current rows and the over-claims (now mostly fixed) are on renderer-contract, render-targets and the modern-GPU evidence page. The residue added is a re-verified account of the former 'hybrid' routes: what SDL_GPU, WebGPU, OpenGL4, EasyGL and Vulkan do when a declaration lacks a semantic the stock effect reads, contrasted with XNA's VerifyCanDraw.

| Concept | Section | Disposition | Destination | TARGET check | Evidence |

## aux-audit-testing-verification (aux)

Alpha.1-era (2026-08-11) audit of CNA's test registration, oracles, pixel/golden testing, Wine/Proton and browser verification, sanitizers, CI and the scripts/ catalogue. The verification deep dives and the Development testing pages already carry almost all of it at 009d40f5, with counts, CI scope and the one-renderer-per-configure claim corrected and every retired-renderer gate removed.
